newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares recover from dip in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares recover from dip in nervous trade.

text.p: Most leading Russian shares recovered from an early-morning dip on Monday that traders said was caused by anxiety that the market was overheating but compensated for by fund flows.
They gave mixed opinion on the strength of the support and shares were mixed midday but operators said there would be no strong fluctuations on the market.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened up 0.46 percent at a record 497.84.
Western support was seen behind the rise of utility Mosenergo which rose to rose to $1.675 at 1001 GMT from $1.64 at Friday's close.
Oil producer LUKoil edged up to $23.43 from $23.40, Rostelekom telecoms company was $5.020 after $5.030 and national electricity company UES rose to $0.480 from $0.463.

"The fall has been fully compensated for and is unlikely to continue today," said Bank Menatep trade department head Sergei Kosynkin. "Athough everything is priced very high, the market has potential for a couple of days more."
Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin said investors would begin seeking out second-tier shares which are less well known later this week.
"There will be less activity in the leading shares, but there will be no fall," Galperin said.
IFCI-Moscow Partner trader Ivan Deryabin said many Russian operators considered many shares too dear for buying.
"In the morning one could feel the depth of the market and small brokers' nervousness," he said. "Everything is expensive now and the market will not close higher than on Friday."
